claims.text: Incorporating dynamic amorphization, grain-boundary dynamics, and nanocrystalline-layer formation into predictive models will improve identification of high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity relative to conventional ab initio or bulk-averaging approaches.
CoCrFeMnNi is a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
CoCrFeMnNi can be synthesized in an initially coarse-grained state.
The grain size and boundary characteristics of the proposed single-phase HEAs can be systematically controlled.
Dynamic amorphization leads to ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layers.
Ultra-high-vacuum or inert conditions limit oxidation and extrinsic oxide-film formation.
CoCrFeMnNi can develop an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer from an initially coarse-grained state.
Grain boundaries serve as effective phonon-scattering centers in the proposed HEAs.
Dynamically induced ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layers serve as effective phonon-scattering centers.
Increasing grain-boundary density enhances phonon scattering.
Dynamic amorphous regions enhance phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering reduces phonon mean free paths and consequently lowers thermal conductivity.

HEAs selected by the proposed approach will have measured phonon thermal conductivities approximately 10–20% below values predicted by traditional ab initio methods that omit microstructural dynamics.
Traditional phonon-thermal-conductivity models rely on bulk properties and ab initio calculations without explicitly representing evolving microstructural features such as dynamic amorphization.
The proposed approach is applicable primarily to single-phase HEAs with controllable grain structures.
Multiphase systems or systems dominated by oxidation and extrinsic surface effects may not show the predicted improvement.
The magnitude of the predicted improvement may vary with alloy composition, processing conditions, and the extent of dynamic amorphization.
The relationship between the proposed microstructural features and phonon transport requires further experimental validation.
Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction of at least 10% relative to conventional-model predictions would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to find a clear association between the specified microstructural features and lower thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.
